facts.text: Evidence: the financial covenant is described as a springing secured net leverage test, "a secured net leverage ratio not to exceed 4.25:1.00" (10-Q June 30, 2026, page:23), tested only when revolver usage exceeds the stated share of commitments. Source risk mechanism: the only leverage ratio the pack reports is total net leverage under the credit agreement definition, "Net leverage as calculated under Post’s credit agreement 4.6x" (EX-99.1 August 2026, page:22), which uses principal debt less cash and a different numerator. No secured net leverage figure is printed in any source. Downstream consequence: CP-1 can show the reported total ratio and the stated covenant level, but cannot compute covenant headroom, and CP-2 must not describe headroom as measured.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is usable and internally consistent. The audited FY2025 statements, three quarterly statements and three earnings releases tie: the September 30, 2025 cash, total assets and long-term debt agree across the 10-K and the 10-Q comparatives, release figures for net earnings, interest and depreciation agree with the filed statements, and the twelve-month figures in the Q3 release reproduce from filed numbers (calculation 1). On the company's own adjusted EBITDA, leverage was 4.84x total and 4.73x net at September 30, 2025, dipped to 4.69x and 4.53x at March 31, 2026, and rose again to 4.75x and 4.59x at June 30, 2026 as Q3 adjusted EBITDA fell 5.0% against Q3 FY2025 while debt stayed at 7,676.0. Adjusted EBITDA is generous: it adds back 232.9 of items over the twelve months (14.4% of the total), including 83.0 of stock-based compensation and 43.3 of losses on held-for-sale assets, and unadjusted operating profit plus depreciation and amortization is 1,378.4, which puts total debt at 5.57x (calculation 5). The company reports 4.6x net leverage under its credit agreement definition and 3.8x interest coverage. Debt is almost entirely fixed-rate notes at a weighted average of 5.5%, of which 1,000.0 is secured, liquidity is 1,242.4, and the first maturity is the 575.0 convertible in August 2027. The main credit-relevant pattern is capital allocation: 916.1 of cash buybacks in nine months against 401.5 of free cash flow was funded by 424.2 of disposal proceeds and a net 223.8 of new debt. Full FY2026 guidance implies a weaker fourth quarter than a year earlier (calculation 8). The base does not support covenant headroom, guarantor-level, legal-term or post-June 30, 2026 conclusions.

facts.text: The only maintenance test is a secured net leverage ratio not to exceed 4.25:1.00, measured at fiscal quarter end only if revolving loans, swing line loans and letter of credit obligations exceed 30% of revolving commitments (Q3 10-Q page:23; Q3 10-Q page:41). At June 30, 2026 usage was 23.2 of letters of credit and no borrowings, against a trigger of 300.0 (calculation 6), so the test was not engaged. The reported figure is total net leverage of 4.6x on credit agreement EBITDA of 1,597.3, which is a different measure from the covenant. Event-of-default cross default and judgment thresholds are 125.0 (page:21). Headroom to the 4.25:1.00 test is Not calculable: the secured net debt numerator and the credit agreement EBITDA definition are not supplied (CP-0 limitation confirmed). An indicative secured-only calculation is in calculation 7 and must not be read as covenant headroom.

Net earnings 335.7 + 242.1 - 284.7 = 293.1 (equals printed). Operating cash flow 998.3 + 691.3 - 697.0 = 992.6. Capital expenditures 510.2 + 289.8 - 360.5 = 439.5. Free cash flow 992.6 - 439.5 = 553.1. Treasury stock purchases 709.0 + 916.1 - 434.3 = 1,190.8. Adjusted EBITDA 1,538.8 + 1,190.5 - 1,113.4 = 1,615.9 (equals printed). 2. Leverage by date. Net debt = principal debt - cash. Sep 30, 2025: 7,452.2 - 176.7 = 7,275.5; 7,452.2 / 1,538.8 = 4.84; 7,275.5 / 1,538.8 = 4.73. Dec 31, 2025: LTM Adjusted EBITDA 1,538.8 + 418.2 - 369.9 = 1,587.1; net debt 7,507.2 - 279.3 = 7,227.9; 7,507.2 / 1,587.1 = 4.73; 7,227.9 / 1,587.1 = 4.55. Net debt issuance 9M FY2026 = 2,265.0 - 2,041.2 = 223.8, and principal debt moved 7,452.2 to 7,676.0, a change of 223.8. Buybacks less free cash flow = 916.1 - 401.5 = 514.6. 4. Adjusted EBITDA build, LTM: 293.1 + 419.1 + 100.4 + 570.4 = 1,383.0; add-backs 1,615.9 - 1,383.0 = 232.9; 232.9 / 1,615.9 = 14.4%. Covenant trigger: 30% x 1,000.0 = 300.0; usage at Jun 30, 2026 = 0.0 borrowings + 23.2 letters of credit = 23.2 (letters of credit may be partly excepted under the credit agreement; not stated). 7. Indicative secured leverage, not the covenant: secured principal 1,000.0 (6.25% senior secured notes; revolver undrawn) less cash 265.6 = 734.4; 734.4 / 1,597.3 = 0.46x. Whether leaseback liabilities are secured and how cash is netted are not supplied. 8. Guidance read-through: FY2026 guidance 1,560 to 1,570 less 9M FY2026 1,190.5 implies Q4 FY2026 of 369.5 to 379.5. Q4 FY2025 = 1,538.8 - 1,113.4 = 425.4, so the implied Q4 is lower by 45.9 to 55.9. 9. Coupon run-rate on the notes at June 30, 2026: 575.0 x 2.50% + 1,385.4 x 4.625% + 980.6 x 4.50% + 1,000.0 x 6.25% + 1,200.0 x 6.375% + 1,200.0 x 6.250% + 1,300.0 x 6.50% = 14.4 + 64.1 + 44.1 + 62.5 + 76.5 + 75.0 + 84.5 = 421.1 (rounded). LTM Adjusted EBITDA 1,615.9 / 421.1 = 3.84x. facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Post is a decentralised, acquisition-built food holding company with four reportable segments: Post Consumer Brands, Weetabix, Foodservice and Refrigerated Retail. For fiscal 2025 the 10-K reports cereal and granola at 32.4% of consolidated net sales, eggs and egg products at 29.6% and pet food at 19.2% (10-K page:11). Each segment depends on a few large customers, Walmart alone being 17.4% of consolidated net sales (10-K page:16). Operating pressure is concentrated in cereal and pet food volumes, while Foodservice earnings have been lifted by avian influenza pricing that management says is about 60 million above the segment's normalised annual run rate (Q3 release page:7). The credit-relevant history is a continuing churn of the perimeter: the full purchase of 8th Avenue on July 1, 2025, the sales of the pasta business on December 1, 2025 and of Crystal Farms on May 1, 2026, and in fiscal 2026 the refinancing of 5.50% notes with 6.50% notes and the add-on of 6.250% notes. Ownership is public with no sponsor, no controlling holder identified in the pack and no sponsor behaviour to assess; the shareholder-ownership table is not in the pack because the annual report incorporates it from the proxy statement by reference. Documented capital allocation shows heavy share repurchases relative to free cash flow, which is a leverage and liquidity mechanic rather than a control-rights finding. No transaction is pending in the sources. Subsequent to the quarter, only further buybacks and narrowed guidance are documented. The business is well documented; ownership, control rights and legal capacity are not.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: All transactions below are completed and documented in filings; no pending transaction, sponsor, merger or LBO is in the pack, and no offering document is supplied, so use of proceeds is taken from the notes to the financial statements. In fiscal 2025, Post issued 600.0 of 6.250% senior notes due October 2034 on October 9, 2024 and used part of the proceeds to redeem the remaining 5.625% notes due January 2028 (10-K page:136). It bought Potato Products of Idaho on March 3, 2025 for 120.0 with cash on hand, and on July 1, 2025 acquired the preferred stock and the 39.5% common equity it did not own in 8th Avenue for a preliminary purchase price of 798.8, which included retiring all 8th Avenue debt other than leaseback financial liabilities, and assumed 111.4 of leaseback financial liabilities (10-K page:117, page:118). In fiscal 2026, Post sold the pasta business on December 1, 2025 for a preliminary 375.0 with closing proceeds of 378.5, and the buyer assumed 78.2 of leaseback financial liabilities, leaving 33.2 of leaseback liabilities in Post's debt, as CP-1 shows (Q3 10-Q page:10). On December 15, 2025 it issued 1,300.0 of 6.50% senior notes due March 2036 at par for net proceeds of 1,284.7 and redeemed all 1,235.0 of its 5.50% notes due December 2029, paying 22.6 of premiums and recording a 17.5 loss on extinguishment (Q3 10-Q page:19, page:22). On March 13, 2026 it issued a further 600.0 of 6.250% notes due October 2034 at 100.75% of par, received 600.4 and repaid the revolver balance, using the remainder for general corporate purposes (Q3 10-Q page:20). It sold Crystal Farms on May 1, 2026 for a preliminary 50.0 with closing proceeds of 45.7, after writing the business down by 43.3 across the nine months, and sold the Sparks Facility for a gain of 21.6 (Q3 10-Q page:12). The liquidity effect, shown in CP-1, is a revolver that moved from 440.0 drawn at September 30, 2025 to undrawn, cash of 265.6 and principal debt 223.8 higher than at September 30, 2025, with the first maturity now the 575.0 convertible in August 2027. Post's shares are repurchased under an authorization of up to 600.0 effective May 9, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:48), with 490.7 remaining on August 5, 2026 (Q3 release page:6). The creditor reading is that the refinancing extended maturities and cleared the revolver, but at a higher coupon on the replaced notes, and that net proceeds from sales were more than spent on repurchases.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: cereal and granola, and pet food, together were 51.6% of fiscal 2025 net sales (32.4% plus 19.2%; 10-K page:11), the 10-K states the cereal category "has experienced weakness, and we expect this trend to continue" (page:16), and Q3 FY2026 Post Consumer Brands volumes excluding 8th Avenue fell 7.1% (Q3 release page:4). Risk mechanic: fixed-cost manufacturing platforms lose absorption when volumes fall, and private label and category competition limit pricing. Credit implication: debt service capacity depends on Foodservice and acquisitions offsetting core volume loss, so refinancing in 2027 and later rests on holding Adjusted EBITDA near the guided level. Category: Analyst Interpretation on cited facts. Counter-evidence: Post Consumer Brands segment Adjusted EBITDA rose 11.2% in Q3 with 8th Avenue included (Q3 release page:4). 2. Earnings quality in Foodservice. Evidence: Q3 declines "reflect the lapping of avian influenza pricing in the prior year period" (Q3 release page:4) and FY2026 guidance includes about 60 million of Foodservice earnings above a 500 million run rate (page:7). Risk mechanic: egg prices spike with disease and revert, so the segment's contribution is cyclical and partly a pricing windfall. Credit implication: reported leverage of 4.6x on the credit agreement basis is on a peak-influenced denominator, and management's own comparable entry level for fiscal 2027 is about 1.48 billion, below the guided fiscal 2026 range. Category: Management Language for the run-rate figures. Counter-evidence: Foodservice volumes rose 4.3% in Q3. 3. Concentration. Evidence: Walmart is 17.4% of consolidated net sales, and the top two customers are 42.0% of Foodservice and 34.9% of Refrigerated Retail (10-K page:16). Risk mechanic: the loss of distribution or a price concession at one customer hits volume and margin across segments simultaneously. Credit implication: concentration raises downside tail risk under the 4.6x leverage. Category: Documentary Fact with Analyst Interpretation of mechanism. 4. Capital allocation. Evidence: buybacks of 916.1 against free cash flow of 401.5 (CP-1). Risk mechanic: debt is not falling while interest expense, net rose 22% in nine months. Credit implication: leverage reduction depends on earnings growth, not repayment, and the Q4 implied by guidance is lower than a year earlier (CP-1 calculation 8). Category: Analyst Interpretation. 5. Portfolio churn. Evidence: two business disposals (pasta, Crystal Farms) and a facility sale within five months, two acquisitions in the prior fiscal year, and integration, transaction and restructuring add-backs recurring in every period (CP-1). Risk mechanic: add-backs labelled non-recurring recur, so Adjusted EBITDA overstates repeatable cash earnings. Credit implication: use the unadjusted sensitivity of 5.57x total debt to operating profit plus depreciation and amortization (CP-1) alongside the 4.75x adjusted figure. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

Evidence: two business disposals (pasta, Crystal Farms) and a facility sale within five months, two acquisitions in the prior fiscal year, and integration, transaction and restructuring add-backs recurring in every period (CP-1). Risk mechanic: add-backs labelled non-recurring recur, so Adjusted EBITDA overstates repeatable cash earnings. Credit implication: use the unadjusted sensitivity of 5.57x total debt to operating profit plus depreciation and amortization (CP-1) alongside the 4.75x adjusted figure. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Post Holdings is a highly leveraged but liquid food producer whose credit depends on holding earnings steady while it chooses between buybacks and debt reduction. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 1,242.4 million, no revolver drawings, fixed-rate notes averaging 5.5%, and no principal due until the USD 575.0 million convertible in August 2027. The weakest point is leverage of 4.59x net and 4.75x total on adjusted EBITDA (5.57x total on unadjusted earnings), with interest cost rising faster than earnings and buybacks above free cash flow. The outcome is decided by whether adjusted EBITDA stays near the guided USD 1,560 to 1,570 million for fiscal 2026 and the roughly USD 1.48 billion comparable level management gives for fiscal 2027, and whether cash is redirected from repurchases to repayment before the 2027 maturity.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Post's financial risk is high but its near-term liquidity risk is low. At June 30, 2026 principal debt was USD 7,676.0 million and net debt USD 7,410.4 million, which is 4.75x and 4.59x twelve-month adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,615.9 million, and 5.57x total debt on operating profit plus depreciation and amortization of USD 1,378.4 million [CP-1 leverage chart and financials table; Documentary Fact for the figures, Analyst Interpretation for the reading]. Leverage was 4.84x total at September 30, 2025 and has moved little since, because the debt added in the period was offset by earnings growth rather than repayment [CP-1 leverage chart; Analyst Interpretation].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Interest is the pressure point. Interest expense, net was USD 419.1 million over the twelve months and rose 22% in the nine months to June 30, 2026 against the prior-year nine months, while third-quarter adjusted EBITDA fell 5.0%. The company-reported interest coverage under its credit agreement fell from 4.1x at March 31, 2026 to 3.8x at June 30, 2026 [CP-1 interest cover chart; Documentary Fact]. Coupons on the notes now run at about USD 421.1 million a year, so interest cover is unlikely to recover without earnings growth or repayment [CP-1 calculation 9; Analyst Interpretation].

facts.text: Capital allocation is the main discretionary lever and is being used for shareholders. Treasury stock purchases of USD 916.1 million in nine months exceeded free cash flow of USD 401.5 million by USD 514.6 million, a gap met from USD 424.2 million of disposal proceeds and USD 223.8 million of net new debt [CP-1 cash flow section; CP-1A governance behaviour; Documentary Fact]. A new share repurchase authorization of USD 600.0 million was approved in May 2026 and USD 490.7 million remained on August 5, 2026 [CP-1A transaction summary; Documentary Fact]. This is rated Neutral or Mixed on governance because it is documented as a shareholder-return choice, not as a transfer away from creditors, but it means the leverage trajectory depends on management discretion rather than on a commitment to repay.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. First, liquidity: USD 1,242.4 million of cash and undrawn revolver, a revolver that matures in February 2029 and sits undrawn, and no principal due before August 2027 [CP-1 liquidity and maturity charts; Documentary Fact]. Second, the debt structure: principal debt of USD 7,676.0 million is almost entirely fixed-rate notes at a weighted average of 5.5%, only USD 1,000.0 million (13.0% of principal, calculated below) is secured, and maturities beyond 2027 are spread across fiscal 2030 to 2036 [CP-1 debt by instrument; Documentary Fact]. Third, cash generation: free cash flow was USD 401.5 million in nine months and USD 553.1 million over twelve months, covering about 7.2% of principal debt a year [CP-1 financials table and calculation 1; Documentary Fact, ratio calculated here]. Fourth, diversification: four segments with segment adjusted EBITDA of USD 197.3 million in Post Consumer Brands, USD 140.8 million in Foodservice, USD 37.3 million in Weetabix and USD 26.6 million in Refrigerated Retail in the third quarter, so no single segment carries the whole result [CP-1 segments table; Documentary Fact]. Fifth, a covenant structure with no regularly tested leverage test while the revolver is lightly used [CP-1 covenants section; Documentary Fact].

First, leverage: 4.59x net and 4.75x total on adjusted EBITDA, 5.57x total on unadjusted earnings, with little progress since September 30, 2025 [CP-1; Documentary Fact, Analyst Interpretation]. rows.label: Post is a large food company that is highly leveraged but liquid. Net debt is 4.59x adjusted EBITDA, interest costs are rising and buybacks outran free cash flow, while USD 1,242.4 million of liquidity limits near-term risk.
Net debt of USD 7,410.4 million is 4.59x twelve-month adjusted EBITDA, and total debt is 4.75x.
Interest expense, net rose 22% in the nine months, and reported coverage fell from 4.1x to 3.8x between March and June 2026.
Buybacks of USD 916.1 million exceeded free cash flow of USD 401.5 million in nine months.
Liquidity is USD 1,242.4 million, and the first maturity is the USD 575.0 million convertible in August 2027.
Cereal and pet food volumes are falling, and Foodservice earnings include temporary avian influenza pricing.

Elevated credit risk on leverage and earnings durability, mitigated by strong near-term liquidity and a long-dated, mostly unsecured fixed-rate debt stack. Credit quality over the next twelve months turns on earnings holding at the guided level and on capital allocation.
Adjusted EBITDA quality and perimeter change
Executed indentures, credit agreement and intercreditor terms not supplied (inherited from the source readiness and financial base)
Secured net leverage ratio not reported; credit agreement EBITDA definition unexplained
Cash interest paid is available only for FY2025
Ownership table, control rights and any rating or agency view not in the pack
No data after June 30, 2026 other than buybacks to August 5, 2026 and narrowed guidance
Adjusted EBITDA is management's non-GAAP measure; the credit agreement adjustment of (18.6) is unexplained

Run settings (from the context file, which is not issuer evidence): reporting currency USD; current period `q3-2026`, prior period `fy-2025`. ### Readiness view

The effective source set is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for the requested pathway. Every source is a filed statement or an issuer earnings release for one legal entity, Post Holdings, Inc., reported on a consolidated basis, and the periods line up with the run: the latest annual report covers the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025 and the latest quarterly report covers the quarter ended June 30, 2026. Filed statements control the figures; the earnings releases are issuer presentations that supply attributed adjusted measures, guidance and the net leverage and interest coverage reconciliation, and they never override a filing. No source is blocked, no identity boundary is unresolved, and nothing in the pack is dated after the cutoff. The limits are missing source types, not unreadable evidence: there are no executed financing documents, no ratings or market data, no investor presentations and nothing after the third quarter release. Those limits restrict legal, covenant and valuation analysis but do not prevent the four selected modules from running. Source sufficiency is not evaluated here for model-input acceptance: the assertion is SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY, CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED.
### Source-by-source assessment
| Source | Document family and authority | Entity and perimeter | Period and basis | Located evidence (exact quote, page) |

### Version relationships

The three 10-Qs and the 10-K are separate periodic reports, not drafts or duplicates of each other, and all stay active. Each 10-Q repeats the September 30, 2025 balance sheet as its comparative, so the 10-K and later 10-Qs overlap on that date; the 10-K is the audited source for September 30, 2025 and the 10-Qs are consistent copies, for example the same total assets figure appears in all four filings. No amendment (10-K/A or 10-Q/A), waiver or supplement is present, and none is referred to in the text read. The three earnings releases each cover the same quarter as one of the 10-Qs; they are companions with different authority (issuer presentation versus filed statement), not duplicates. Releases disclose adjusted measures that the filings do not.
### Entity roles and perimeter

Borrower, issuer and parent are the same entity: Post Holdings, Inc. The text states that the revolving credit agreement is guaranteed and secured by subsidiaries and that senior notes are guaranteed by domestic subsidiaries, for example: "are secured by security interests in substantially all of our assets and the assets of our subsidiary guarantors, but excluding, in each case, real property" (10-Q June 30, 2026, page:39). The sources do not name the guarantor subsidiaries, the excluded subsidiaries or any unrestricted subsidiary, and do not give guarantor-only financial information. Consolidated statements include a noncontrolling interest (Weetabix East Africa and Alpen are described in the 10-Q June 30, 2026 notes, page:8), which is shown as a separate equity line and means consolidated figures are not all attributable to the borrower group. These distinctions stay open as gaps.
### Consumer assessment
| Consumer | Status | Evidence demanded and located | Limitation carried |

| CP-1A (business and transaction context) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Business description, segments, acquisitions, divestitures and capital allocation are present in the 10-K and quarterly notes. Divestitures: "On December 1, 2025, the Company completed its previously announced sale of 8th Avenue’s pasta business" (10-Q June 30, 2026, page:10); "On May 1, 2026, the Company completed the sale of substantially all of the assets of" the Crystal Farms Business (page:12). Guidance: "Narrowed fiscal year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP)* outlook to $1,560-$1,570 million" (EX-99.1 August 2026, page:2). | Public listed company with no sponsor and no pending financing transaction document; no investor presentations or management prepared remarks; guidance is management language. |

| CP-2 (fundamental credit synthesis) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Draws only on upstream handoffs from CP-1 and CP-1A, which the sources support. | No rating, market or peer context (context blank); inherits all CP-1 and CP-1A limits. A missing upstream handoff is not a source condition. |

| CP-5 (evidence trace validation) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Needs the pinned sources to test cited quotes and cross-module figures; all seven are text-extracted and quotable. | Extraction fidelity of tables was not independently reviewed; checks are limited to the supplied text. |
### Coverage statement

All seven sources were extracted to text with 378 chunks in total, namely 169 for the 10-K, 43, 51 and 50 for the three 10-Qs, and 19, 24 and 22 for the three releases. Every source was read for identity, period and statement content; no chunk is marked blocked. Each coverage unit is retained as evidence, recorded as a gap in the Gaps section, or ignored with a basis (only `_retrieval.json`, which is pack metadata). The 10-K contains the audit report (page:91 to page:94), the full statements (page:94 to page:98), the long-term debt note (page:131 to page:142) and the exhibit index (page:163 to page:168). Short chunks, such as page:101 or page:111 of the 10-K, are page-break splits within tables or notes and the neighbouring chunks carry the remainder. This is text extraction only: no chart, image or presentation slide was inspected, and a successful extraction is not a fidelity review.
### Strongest contrary evidence and limitations

Evidence: the financial covenant is described as a springing secured net leverage test, "a secured net leverage ratio not to exceed 4.25:1.00" (10-Q June 30, 2026, page:23), tested only when revolver usage exceeds the stated share of commitments. Source risk mechanism: the only leverage ratio the pack reports is total net leverage under the credit agreement definition, "Net leverage as calculated under Post’s credit agreement 4.6x" (EX-99.1 August 2026, page:22), which uses principal debt less cash and a different numerator. No secured net leverage figure is printed in any source. Downstream consequence: CP-1 can show the reported total ratio and the stated covenant level, but cannot compute covenant headroom, and CP-2 must not describe headroom as measured.

Evidence: the debt note lists each instrument, but guarantee, security and call terms are given only in summary, and the 10-K exhibit index lists the governing documents, for example "4.1 Indenture (2029 Notes), dated as of July 3, 2019" (10-K, page:163), without including them. Source risk mechanism: summary note text is a filed statement but is not the executed document, so definitions, baskets, restricted payment capacity and release mechanics cannot be tested. Downstream consequence: legal, intercreditor and restricted-payment conclusions are not supportable from this pack; share repurchases are large and are disclosed ("Subsequent to the end of the third quarter of fiscal year 2026 through August 5, 2026, Post repurchased 0.4 million shares for $39.3 million", EX-99.1 August 2026, page:6), so the missing capacity definitions matter.

Evidence: the latest balance sheet is June 30, 2026 and the latest source is dated August 6, 2026, while the as-of date is November 5, 2026. Source risk mechanism: leverage, liquidity and share count may have moved since; the only post-quarter fact is the repurchase through August 5, 2026. Downstream consequence: the current period is the quarter ended June 30, 2026, and any statement about the position at the as-of date is outside the evidence.
### Conflicts and anomalies

1. Release dates against file names. The first quarter release file is labelled 2026-02-03, but the text reads "Post Holdings Reports Results for the First Quarter of Fiscal Year 2026; Raises Fiscal Year 2026 Outlook St. Louis - February 5, 2026" (EX-99.1_2026-02-03, page:2). The second quarter release file is labelled 2026-05-05, but the text reads "St. Louis - May 7, 2026" (EX-99.1_2026-05-05, page:2). The document text controls: use February 5, 2026 and May 7, 2026 as release dates. Both are well before the cutoff, so no cutoff effect.
2. Fiscal naming. File names such as `ex99-1q12026er` describe the fiscal first quarter, which ends December 31, 2025, not a calendar first quarter. Downstream labels must follow the document text.
## Calculations

None. CP-0 performs no calculation, normalisation or reconciliation. Every number quoted above is copied from a source as printed, with its locator. Ratios and sums are left to the downstream modules.

spans.text: ## Request

Issuer: Post Holdings, Inc. (POST), a single consolidated reporting entity, borrower of the credit agreement and issuer of all senior notes. As-of date: 2026-11-05; evidence cutoff 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit_snapshot. Reporting currency: USD, in millions as the filings print them.

Scope of this module: extract and organise the financial base for the later modules: statements, the adjusted EBITDA definition, debt by instrument, liquidity, covenant, cash flow, claims outside debt and subsequent events, with leverage, interest cover, liquidity and maturity chart data. Periods follow Post's fiscal year, which ends September 30: FY2025 is the year ended September 30, 2025 (context prior period `fy-2025`); the current period `q3-2026` is the fiscal third quarter ended June 30, 2026, with nine months (9M) fiscal 2026 and the twelve months (LTM) ended June 30, 2026. Quarters are labelled by fiscal quarter, so Q1 FY2026 ended December 31, 2025 and Q2 FY2026 ended March 31, 2026. Sources and context agree on currency and periods, so there is no mismatch to report.

Correction to the earlier source-readiness handoff (CP-0, which cannot be edited): it said the reported total net leverage "uses principal debt less cash and a different numerator". Stated precisely, the release defines that ratio as principal debt less cash and cash equivalents over credit-agreement-adjusted Adjusted EBITDA for the last twelve months (EX-99.1 August 2026, page:17 and page:22), and the covenant ratio is a secured net leverage ratio whose numerator definition is not supplied. Nothing else in that handoff is changed.
## Sources
### Issuer sources relied on
| Source (exact name) | sha256 |
| 10-Q_2025-12-31_post-20251231.htm.jsonl | e9cc6f62805c1b1bab9b7edb1afd055ae5b09d286a5f5385add48be2adcd1950 |
| EX-99.1_2026-05-05_ex99-1q22026er.htm.jsonl | c699bde5529dd39cf184dac3c7c6fd8e1af3530dddd1b671a659bdd669e9f846 |

In locators below, "10-K" is the FY2025 annual report, "Q1 10-Q", "Q2 10-Q" and "Q3 10-Q" are the quarterly reports for December 31, 2025, March 31, 2026 and June 30, 2026, and "Q1 release", "Q2 release" and "Q3 release" are the matching EX-99.1 earnings releases.
### Supplied handoffs

CP-0 rated the source set READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for this module. Its limits are carried here: no executed financing documents, no secured net leverage figure, no cash interest paid for interim periods in the 10-Qs (searched here, see Gaps), no balance sheet after June 30, 2026, and no ratings or market data. The release file dates for Q1 and Q2 differ from the dates printed in the releases (February 5 and May 7, 2026); neither affects any figure.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Leverage is high and has barely improved: net debt is about 4.6 times adjusted EBITDA, interest cost is rising faster than earnings, and shareholder buybacks absorbed more cash than free cash flow. Liquidity is ample. | Medium | Adjusted EBITDA is management's measure, cash interest is only available for FY2025, and the covenant metric is not reported. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Total debt was 7,676.0 and net debt 7,410.4 at June 30, 2026, against twelve-month adjusted EBITDA of 1,615.9. | Net leverage of 4.59x on this basis, and total leverage of 4.75x, leave limited room for earnings shortfalls. | Medium |

| Interest expense, net rose 22% in both Q3 and the nine months while Q3 adjusted EBITDA fell 5.0%. | Reported interest coverage under the credit agreement fell from 4.1x to 3.8x between March and June 2026. | High |

| Cash plus undrawn revolver was 1,242.4 at June 30, 2026; the revolver of 1,000.0 matures in February 2029 and is undrawn. | Near-term liquidity is strong; the 575.0 convertible notes due August 2027 are the first maturity. | High |

| Nine-month buybacks of 916.1 exceeded free cash flow of 401.5; debt rose 223.8 despite 424.2 of disposal proceeds. | Leverage reduction is being deprioritised in favour of share repurchases. | High |

| The only maintenance covenant found is a springing secured leverage test, not applied while revolver usage stays below 30% of commitments. | Covenant protection is thin, and headroom cannot be measured from the pack. | Medium |
### Financial base view

The financial base is usable and internally consistent. The audited FY2025 statements, three quarterly statements and three earnings releases tie: the September 30, 2025 cash, total assets and long-term debt agree across the 10-K and the 10-Q comparatives, release figures for net earnings, interest and depreciation agree with the filed statements, and the twelve-month figures in the Q3 release reproduce from filed numbers (calculation 1). On the company's own adjusted EBITDA, leverage was 4.84x total and 4.73x net at September 30, 2025, dipped to 4.69x and 4.53x at March 31, 2026, and rose again to 4.75x and 4.59x at June 30, 2026 as Q3 adjusted EBITDA fell 5.0% against Q3 FY2025 while debt stayed at 7,676.0. Adjusted EBITDA is generous: it adds back 232.9 of items over the twelve months (14.4% of the total), including 83.0 of stock-based compensation and 43.3 of losses on held-for-sale assets, and unadjusted operating profit plus depreciation and amortization is 1,378.4, which puts total debt at 5.57x (calculation 5). The company reports 4.6x net leverage under its credit agreement definition and 3.8x interest coverage. Debt is almost entirely fixed-rate notes at a weighted average of 5.5%, of which 1,000.0 is secured, liquidity is 1,242.4, and the first maturity is the 575.0 convertible in August 2027. The main credit-relevant pattern is capital allocation: 916.1 of cash buybacks in nine months against 401.5 of free cash flow was funded by 424.2 of disposal proceeds and a net 223.8 of new debt. Full FY2026 guidance implies a weaker fourth quarter than a year earlier (calculation 8). The base does not support covenant headroom, guarantor-level, legal-term or post-June 30, 2026 conclusions.

After June 30, 2026 the pack shows only the 0.4 million share repurchase for 39.3 through August 5, 2026 and the narrowed FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance of 1,560 to 1,570, down from a range of 1,550 to 1,580 (Q3 release page:6). ## Calculations
3. Net debt issuance 9M FY2026 = 2,265.0 - 2,041.2 = 223.8, and principal debt moved 7,452.2 to 7,676.0, a change of 223.8. Buybacks less free cash flow = 916.1 - 401.5 = 514.6.

5. Unadjusted EBITDA = operating profit + D&A. FY2025: 799.3 + 524.3 = 1,323.6. LTM: 808.0 + 570.4 = 1,378.4. 9M FY2026: 639.6 + 424.2 = 1,063.8. 9M FY2025: 630.9 + 378.1 = 1,009.0. Leverage: 7,676.0 / 1,378.4 = 5.57; 7,452.2 / 1,323.6 = 5.63. Difference to Adjusted EBITDA: 1,615.9 - 1,378.4 = 237.5, being add-backs 232.9 plus 4.6 of non-operating items between net earnings-based and operating-profit-based totals (1,383.0 - 1,378.4).
6. Covenant trigger: 30% x 1,000.0 = 300.0; usage at Jun 30, 2026 = 0.0 borrowings + 23.2 letters of credit = 23.2 (letters of credit may be partly excepted under the credit agreement; not stated).

7. Indicative secured leverage, not the covenant: secured principal 1,000.0 (6.25% senior secured notes; revolver undrawn) less cash 265.6 = 734.4; 734.4 / 1,597.3 = 0.46x. Whether leaseback liabilities are secured and how cash is netted are not supplied.
8. Guidance read-through: FY2026 guidance 1,560 to 1,570 less 9M FY2026 1,190.5 implies Q4 FY2026 of 369.5 to 379.5. Q4 FY2025 = 1,538.8 - 1,113.4 = 425.4, so the implied Q4 is lower by 45.9 to 55.9.

9. Coupon run-rate on the notes at June 30, 2026: 575.0 x 2.50% + 1,385.4 x 4.625% + 980.6 x 4.50% + 1,000.0 x 6.25% + 1,200.0 x 6.375% + 1,200.0 x 6.250% + 1,300.0 x 6.50% = 14.4 + 64.1 + 44.1 + 62.5 + 76.5 + 75.0 + 84.5 = 421.1 (rounded). LTM Adjusted EBITDA 1,615.9 / 421.1 = 3.84x. This excludes the leaseback (about 3.1 at 9.29%), revolver commitment fees, amortisation and interest income, so it is an approximation of cash coupon only.

11. Interest cover FY2025: 1,538.8 / 370.1 = 4.16; 1,538.8 / 361.4 = 4.26. Company coverage: 1,597.3 / 419.1 = 3.81 (reported 3.8x); 1,646.9 / 399.4 = 4.12 (reported 4.1x). Q3 interest expense, net of 108.2 against 88.5 is +19.7, or 22%; Q3 Adjusted EBITDA 377.3 against 397.0 is -19.7, or -5.0%.

Proceed to CP-1A (business and transaction context), then CP-2 and CP-5. | Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Cereal, granola and pet food were over half of fiscal 2025 sales, and both categories lost volume in the latest quarter. | Core earnings face structural volume pressure, which supports leverage staying high unless other segments offset it. | Medium |

| Foodservice earnings include roughly 60 million above a normalised run rate, driven by avian influenza pricing that is now being lapped. | Earnings quality is flattered, and management itself guides to lower comparable earnings entering fiscal 2027. | Medium |
| Large customers carry heavy shares of each segment, led by Walmart at 17.4% of fiscal 2025 sales. | Customer concentration can move margins and volumes quickly. | High |

| In fiscal 2026 Post refinanced its notes, sold the pasta and Crystal Farms businesses, and repurchased shares well above free cash flow. | Capital allocation favours shareholders over deleveraging, which lengthens the path to lower leverage. | High |
| Post is listed, has no sponsor, and shareholder control rights are not in the pack. | Governance behaviour can be judged only from documented actions, which show no creditor-adverse step. | Low |
### Business and transaction view

Post is a decentralised, acquisition-built food holding company with four reportable segments: Post Consumer Brands, Weetabix, Foodservice and Refrigerated Retail. For fiscal 2025 the 10-K reports cereal and granola at 32.4% of consolidated net sales, eggs and egg products at 29.6% and pet food at 19.2% (10-K page:11). Each segment depends on a few large customers, Walmart alone being 17.4% of consolidated net sales (10-K page:16). Operating pressure is concentrated in cereal and pet food volumes, while Foodservice earnings have been lifted by avian influenza pricing that management says is about 60 million above the segment's normalised annual run rate (Q3 release page:7). The credit-relevant history is a continuing churn of the perimeter: the full purchase of 8th Avenue on July 1, 2025, the sales of the pasta business on December 1, 2025 and of Crystal Farms on May 1, 2026, and in fiscal 2026 the refinancing of 5.50% notes with 6.50% notes and the add-on of 6.250% notes. Ownership is public with no sponsor, no controlling holder identified in the pack and no sponsor behaviour to assess; the shareholder-ownership table is not in the pack because the annual report incorporates it from the proxy statement by reference. Documented capital allocation shows heavy share repurchases relative to free cash flow, which is a leverage and liquidity mechanic rather than a control-rights finding. No transaction is pending in the sources. Subsequent to the quarter, only further buybacks and narrowed guidance are documented. The business is well documented; ownership, control rights and legal capacity are not.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

All transactions below are completed and documented in filings; no pending transaction, sponsor, merger or LBO is in the pack, and no offering document is supplied, so use of proceeds is taken from the notes to the financial statements. In fiscal 2025, Post issued 600.0 of 6.250% senior notes due October 2034 on October 9, 2024 and used part of the proceeds to redeem the remaining 5.625% notes due January 2028 (10-K page:136). It bought Potato Products of Idaho on March 3, 2025 for 120.0 with cash on hand, and on July 1, 2025 acquired the preferred stock and the 39.5% common equity it did not own in 8th Avenue for a preliminary purchase price of 798.8, which included retiring all 8th Avenue debt other than leaseback financial liabilities, and assumed 111.4 of leaseback financial liabilities (10-K page:117, page:118). In fiscal 2026, Post sold the pasta business on December 1, 2025 for a preliminary 375.0 with closing proceeds of 378.5, and the buyer assumed 78.2 of leaseback financial liabilities, leaving 33.2 of leaseback liabilities in Post's debt, as CP-1 shows (Q3 10-Q page:10). On December 15, 2025 it issued 1,300.0 of 6.50% senior notes due March 2036 at par for net proceeds of 1,284.7 and redeemed all 1,235.0 of its 5.50% notes due December 2029, paying 22.6 of premiums and recording a 17.5 loss on extinguishment (Q3 10-Q page:19, page:22). On March 13, 2026 it issued a further 600.0 of 6.250% notes due October 2034 at 100.75% of par, received 600.4 and repaid the revolver balance, using the remainder for general corporate purposes (Q3 10-Q page:20). It sold Crystal Farms on May 1, 2026 for a preliminary 50.0 with closing proceeds of 45.7, after writing the business down by 43.3 across the nine months, and sold the Sparks Facility for a gain of 21.6 (Q3 10-Q page:12). The liquidity effect, shown in CP-1, is a revolver that moved from 440.0 drawn at September 30, 2025 to undrawn, cash of 265.6 and principal debt 223.8 higher than at September 30, 2025, with the first maturity now the 575.0 convertible in August 2027. Post's shares are repurchased under an authorization of up to 600.0 effective May 9, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:48), with 490.7 remaining on August 5, 2026 (Q3 release page:6). The creditor reading is that the refinancing extended maturities and cleared the revolver, but at a higher coupon on the replaced notes, and that net proceeds from sales were more than spent on repurchases.

### Credit translations

1. Revenue durability. Evidence: cereal and granola, and pet food, together were 51.6% of fiscal 2025 net sales (32.4% plus 19.2%; 10-K page:11), the 10-K states the cereal category "has experienced weakness, and we expect this trend to continue" (page:16), and Q3 FY2026 Post Consumer Brands volumes excluding 8th Avenue fell 7.1% (Q3 release page:4). Risk mechanic: fixed-cost manufacturing platforms lose absorption when volumes fall, and private label and category competition limit pricing. Credit implication: debt service capacity depends on Foodservice and acquisitions offsetting core volume loss, so refinancing in 2027 and later rests on holding Adjusted EBITDA near the guided level. Category: Analyst Interpretation on cited facts. Counter-evidence: Post Consumer Brands segment Adjusted EBITDA rose 11.2% in Q3 with 8th Avenue included (Q3 release page:4).

2. Earnings quality in Foodservice. Evidence: Q3 declines "reflect the lapping of avian influenza pricing in the prior year period" (Q3 release page:4) and FY2026 guidance includes about 60 million of Foodservice earnings above a 500 million run rate (page:7). Risk mechanic: egg prices spike with disease and revert, so the segment's contribution is cyclical and partly a pricing windfall. Credit implication: reported leverage of 4.6x on the credit agreement basis is on a peak-influenced denominator, and management's own comparable entry level for fiscal 2027 is about 1.48 billion, below the guided fiscal 2026 range. Category: Management Language for the run-rate figures. Counter-evidence: Foodservice volumes rose 4.3% in Q3.

3. Concentration. Evidence: Walmart is 17.4% of consolidated net sales, and the top two customers are 42.0% of Foodservice and 34.9% of Refrigerated Retail (10-K page:16). Risk mechanic: the loss of distribution or a price concession at one customer hits volume and margin across segments simultaneously. Credit implication: concentration raises downside tail risk under the 4.6x leverage. Category: Documentary Fact with Analyst Interpretation of mechanism.

4. Capital allocation. Evidence: buybacks of 916.1 against free cash flow of 401.5 (CP-1). Risk mechanic: debt is not falling while interest expense, net rose 22% in nine months. Credit implication: leverage reduction depends on earnings growth, not repayment, and the Q4 implied by guidance is lower than a year earlier (CP-1 calculation 8). Category: Analyst Interpretation.

5. Portfolio churn. Evidence: two business disposals (pasta, Crystal Farms) and a facility sale within five months, two acquisitions in the prior fiscal year, and integration, transaction and restructuring add-backs recurring in every period (CP-1). Risk mechanic: add-backs labelled non-recurring recur, so Adjusted EBITDA overstates repeatable cash earnings. Credit implication: use the unadjusted sensitivity of 5.57x total debt to operating profit plus depreciation and amortization (CP-1) alongside the 4.75x adjusted figure. Category: Analyst Interpretation.
Key uncertainties: ownership concentration, executed financing terms, any rating view, and the position after June 30, 2026.

No other conflict between sources was found on transaction size or terms: the pasta business sale is a preliminary price of 375.0 and closing proceeds of 378.5, which differ by definition, not by disagreement.

## Calculations

1. Cereal, granola and pet food share of FY2025 net sales: 32.4% + 19.2% = 51.6% (10-K page:11). These are the filing's percentages and overlap is not stated, so the sum assumes the categories are separate, which the 10-K's product table supports (cereal and granola 2,645.5 and pet food 1,570.4 on separate lines, 10-K page:157).
2. Share of net sales from product lines: cereal and granola 2,645.5 / 8,158.1 = 32.4%; eggs 2,413.1 / 8,158.1 = 29.6%; pet food 1,570.4 / 8,158.1 = 19.2%. These reproduce the printed percentages.
3. Buyback excess over free cash flow: 916.1 - 401.5 = 514.6 (CP-1).
4. Segment net sales check: 4,024.6 + 542.2 + 2,641.0 + 953.3 = 8,161.1, less corporate and eliminations 3.0 = 8,158.1 (10-K page:155).
5. Disposal proceeds: pasta closing proceeds 378.5 + Crystal Farms 45.7 = 424.2, equal to the investing line in CP-1.

6. Leaseback balance after sale: 8th Avenue leaseback liabilities assumed 111.4, less 78.2 assumed by the pasta buyer, is 33.2, equal to the balance in the June 30, 2026 debt table. This reconciles only if no payments reduced the balance, which the single 33.2 balance at both September 30, 2025 and June 30, 2026 indicates (CP-1).

This is the fundamental credit synthesis for Post Holdings, Inc. as of 2026-11-05 (evidence cutoff 2026-11-05), pathway credit_snapshot, in USD. It combines the financial base and the business and transaction context from the earlier handoffs into a credit view, strengths, weaknesses, findings and risks, using the latest filed period, the fiscal third quarter ended June 30, 2026, with the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025 as the prior period. It gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Post is a large food company that is highly leveraged but liquid. Net debt is 4.59x adjusted EBITDA, interest costs are rising and buybacks outran free cash flow, while USD 1,242.4 million of liquidity limits near-term risk. | Medium | Adjusted EBITDA is management's measure, and no legal documents, ratings or ownership detail were supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |
| Net debt of USD 7,410.4 million is 4.59x twelve-month adjusted EBITDA, and total debt is 4.75x. | Leverage is high with limited room for an earnings shortfall. | Medium |
| Interest expense, net rose 22% in the nine months, and reported coverage fell from 4.1x to 3.8x between March and June 2026. | Debt service is absorbing a growing share of earnings. | High |
| Buybacks of USD 916.1 million exceeded free cash flow of USD 401.5 million in nine months. | Deleveraging is not the priority, so leverage falls only if earnings grow. | High |

| Liquidity is USD 1,242.4 million, and the first maturity is the USD 575.0 million convertible in August 2027. | Near-term repayment risk is low, but that maturity falls within twelve months of the as-of date. | High |
| Cereal and pet food volumes are falling, and Foodservice earnings include temporary avian influenza pricing. | Earnings durability is weaker than reported adjusted EBITDA suggests. | Medium |
### Credit view

Post Holdings is a highly leveraged but liquid food producer whose credit depends on holding earnings steady while it chooses between buybacks and debt reduction. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 1,242.4 million, no revolver drawings, fixed-rate notes averaging 5.5%, and no principal due until the USD 575.0 million convertible in August 2027. The weakest point is leverage of 4.59x net and 4.75x total on adjusted EBITDA (5.57x total on unadjusted earnings), with interest cost rising faster than earnings and buybacks above free cash flow. The outcome is decided by whether adjusted EBITDA stays near the guided USD 1,560 to 1,570 million for fiscal 2026 and the roughly USD 1.48 billion comparable level management gives for fiscal 2027, and whether cash is redirected from repurchases to repayment before the 2027 maturity.
### Key findings

Post's financial risk is high but its near-term liquidity risk is low. At June 30, 2026 principal debt was USD 7,676.0 million and net debt USD 7,410.4 million, which is 4.75x and 4.59x twelve-month adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,615.9 million, and 5.57x total debt on operating profit plus depreciation and amortization of USD 1,378.4 million [CP-1 leverage chart and financials table; Documentary Fact for the figures, Analyst Interpretation for the reading]. Leverage was 4.84x total at September 30, 2025 and has moved little since, because the debt added in the period was offset by earnings growth rather than repayment [CP-1 leverage chart; Analyst Interpretation].

Interest is the pressure point. Interest expense, net was USD 419.1 million over the twelve months and rose 22% in the nine months to June 30, 2026 against the prior-year nine months, while third-quarter adjusted EBITDA fell 5.0%. The company-reported interest coverage under its credit agreement fell from 4.1x at March 31, 2026 to 3.8x at June 30, 2026 [CP-1 interest cover chart; Documentary Fact]. Coupons on the notes now run at about USD 421.1 million a year, so interest cover is unlikely to recover without earnings growth or repayment [CP-1 calculation 9; Analyst Interpretation].

Capital allocation is the main discretionary lever and is being used for shareholders. Treasury stock purchases of USD 916.1 million in nine months exceeded free cash flow of USD 401.5 million by USD 514.6 million, a gap met from USD 424.2 million of disposal proceeds and USD 223.8 million of net new debt [CP-1 cash flow section; CP-1A governance behaviour; Documentary Fact]. A new share repurchase authorization of USD 600.0 million was approved in May 2026 and USD 490.7 million remained on August 5, 2026 [CP-1A transaction summary; Documentary Fact]. This is rated Neutral or Mixed on governance because it is documented as a shareholder-return choice, not as a transfer away from creditors, but it means the leverage trajectory depends on management discretion rather than on a commitment to repay.

Liquidity and the debt profile are the main support. Cash of USD 265.6 million and an undrawn USD 1,000.0 million revolver less USD 23.2 million of letters of credit give USD 1,242.4 million of liquidity, 2.2x the USD 575.0 million convertible due August 2027 (calculated below). The revolver matures in February 2029, and the other notes mature between 2030 and 2036 [CP-1 liquidity and maturity charts; Documentary Fact]. The August 2027 convertible falls within twelve months of the as-of date, so its settlement, which Post may make in cash, shares or both, is the first refinancing event to monitor [CP-1 debt table; Analyst Interpretation].

Earnings quality and durability are weaker than the adjusted figures suggest. Adjusted EBITDA includes USD 232.9 million of add-backs, which is 14.4% of the total, among them USD 83.0 million of stock-based compensation, and integration, transaction and restructuring items that recur in every period [CP-1 Adjusted EBITDA review; CP-1A credit translation on portfolio churn; Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation]. Foodservice earnings include roughly USD 60 million above a normalised run rate from avian influenza pricing that is being lapped, and management's own comparable entry level for fiscal 2027 of about USD 1.48 billion sits below guided fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,560 to 1,570 million [CP-1A credit translations 2; Management Language]. Fiscal 2026 guidance implies a fourth quarter of USD 369.5 million to USD 379.5 million, below the USD 425.4 million of the prior-year quarter [CP-1 calculation 8; Analyst Interpretation].

Covenant protection is thin and cannot be measured. The only maintenance test found is a secured net leverage covenant of 4.25:1.00 that applies only when revolver usage exceeds 30% of commitments, a trigger of USD 300.0 million against usage of USD 23.2 million, so the test did not apply at June 30, 2026 [CP-1 covenants section; Documentary Fact]. Headroom is Not calculable because the secured net debt and credit agreement EBITDA definitions were not supplied. The company's reported total net leverage of 4.6x is a different measure and must not be read as covenant headroom [CP-1; CP-1 correction of the earlier wording].
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. First, liquidity: USD 1,242.4 million of cash and undrawn revolver, a revolver that matures in February 2029 and sits undrawn, and no principal due before August 2027 [CP-1 liquidity and maturity charts; Documentary Fact]. Second, the debt structure: principal debt of USD 7,676.0 million is almost entirely fixed-rate notes at a weighted average of 5.5%, only USD 1,000.0 million (13.0% of principal, calculated below) is secured, and maturities beyond 2027 are spread across fiscal 2030 to 2036 [CP-1 debt by instrument; Documentary Fact]. Third, cash generation: free cash flow was USD 401.5 million in nine months and USD 553.1 million over twelve months, covering about 7.2% of principal debt a year [CP-1 financials table and calculation 1; Documentary Fact, ratio calculated here]. Fourth, diversification: four segments with segment adjusted EBITDA of USD 197.3 million in Post Consumer Brands, USD 140.8 million in Foodservice, USD 37.3 million in Weetabix and USD 26.6 million in Refrigerated Retail in the third quarter, so no single segment carries the whole result [CP-1 segments table; Documentary Fact]. Fifth, a covenant structure with no regularly tested leverage test while the revolver is lightly used [CP-1 covenants section; Documentary Fact].

Weaknesses. First, leverage: 4.59x net and 4.75x total on adjusted EBITDA, 5.57x total on unadjusted earnings, with little progress since September 30, 2025 [CP-1; Documentary Fact, Analyst Interpretation]. Second, rising interest burden, with coverage reported at 3.8x and falling [CP-1 interest cover chart; Documentary Fact]. Third, the use of cash: buybacks above free cash flow, with the revolver cleared by new notes rather than by cash from operations [CP-1 cash flow section; CP-1A governance behaviour; Documentary Fact, Analyst Interpretation]. Fourth, volume pressure in the core categories: cereal, granola and pet food were 51.6% of fiscal 2025 net sales, and Post Consumer Brands volumes excluding 8th Avenue fell 7.1% in the third quarter [CP-1A operating model and credit translation 1; Documentary Fact, Analyst Interpretation]. Fifth, customer concentration: Walmart is 17.4% of consolidated net sales, and the two largest customers are 42.0% of Foodservice and 34.9% of Refrigerated Retail [CP-1A credit translation 3; Documentary Fact]. Sixth, adjusted EBITDA quality and perimeter churn, with USD 232.9 million of add-backs and two business sales in five months [CP-1; CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. Seventh, an evidence gap: no executed indentures or credit agreement, no ownership table, no ratings and no data after June 30, 2026, which limits conclusions on legal capacity, control rights and covenant headroom [CP-0 and CP-1A gaps; Insufficient Information].
### Credit assessment
| Assessment | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Elevated credit risk on leverage and earnings durability, mitigated by strong near-term liquidity and a long-dated, mostly unsecured fixed-rate debt stack. Credit quality over the next twelve months turns on earnings holding at the guided level and on capital allocation. | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 leverage, interest cover, liquidity and maturity charts, financials table and cash flow section; CP-1A credit translations 1 to 5 |
### Credit thesis

Post can service and refinance its debt in the near term on liquidity and fixed-rate, long-dated notes, but with net leverage near 4.6x, rising interest costs and buybacks above free cash flow, its credit quality depends on earnings holding up and management choosing to reduce debt.
Category: Analyst Interpretation. Basis: CP-1 and CP-1A as cited above.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity | Category and basis |

| Leverage with limited earnings cushion | Net debt of USD 7,410.4 million is 4.59x adjusted EBITDA; unadjusted total leverage is 5.57x; a fall to the roughly USD 1.48 billion comparable level, at constant net debt, would put net leverage near 5.0x (calculated below) | Refinancing terms and debt service tolerance deteriorate if earnings fall short of guidance | Material | Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 leverage chart, calculation 5; CP-1A translation 2 |

| Rising interest burden | Interest expense, net rose 22% in nine months on higher debt, higher rates and lower interest income; coupon run-rate about USD 421.1 million | Coverage of 3.8x has little buffer, and cash interest only available for FY2025 limits the cash-basis view | Material | Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 interest cover chart, calculation 9 |

| Shareholder-return funded partly by debt | Buybacks of USD 916.1 million versus free cash flow of USD 401.5 million; net new debt of USD 223.8 million | Leverage reduction depends on management discretion; restricted payment capacity unverified | Material | Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 cash flow section; CP-1A governance |

| Core volume decline and concentration | Cereal and pet food volumes falling; Walmart 17.4% of net sales; top-two customers 42.0% and 34.9% in two segments | Fixed-cost absorption falls and negotiating leverage sits with customers, pressuring margins | Material | Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1A operating model and translations 1 and 3 |

| Temporary Foodservice earnings | About USD 60 million above run rate from avian influenza pricing; guided Q4 below prior year | Reported leverage flatters underlying earnings | Material | Management Language and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1A translation 2; CP-1 calculation 8 |

| August 2027 convertible maturity | USD 575.0 million due August 15, 2027, within twelve months of the as-of date; settlement in cash, shares or both at Post's election | Needs refinancing or repayment from liquidity of USD 1,242.4 million, which covers it 2.2x | Minor | Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 maturity chart and debt table |

| Covenant headroom unmeasured | Springing secured leverage test of 4.25:1.00 not applied while revolver usage stays under the 30% trigger; secured net debt not supplied | Protection is limited; compliance is stated by the company but cannot be verified | Minor | Documentary Fact; Insufficient Information on headroom; CP-1 covenants |

| Adjusted EBITDA quality and perimeter change | USD 232.9 million of add-backs including recurring integration and restructuring items; two acquisitions and two business disposals between March 2025 and May 2026 | Comparisons across periods are distorted | Material | Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 EBITDA review; CP-1A translation 5 |
## Calculations
Inputs are CP-1 figures unless stated; results are calculated here and are illustrative.
1. Liquidity coverage of the August 2027 convertible: USD 1,242.4 million / USD 575.0 million = 2.2x.

2. Secured share of principal debt: USD 1,000.0 million / USD 7,676.0 million = 13.0%. This counts only the 6.25% senior secured notes; whether the leaseback financial liabilities of USD 33.2 million are secured is not supplied.
3. Free cash flow yield on principal debt: USD 553.1 million / USD 7,676.0 million = 7.2%.

4. Sensitivity of leverage to management's comparable fiscal 2027 level (management language, not a forecast verified here): USD 7,410.4 million / USD 1,480 million = 5.01x net, and USD 7,676.0 million / USD 1,480 million = 5.19x total, holding debt and cash at June 30, 2026 levels. The coupon run-rate of USD 421.1 million against USD 1,480 million is 3.5x.

5. Illustrative net debt reduction to reach 4.00x net leverage on the same twelve-month adjusted EBITDA: USD 7,410.4 million less 4.00 x USD 1,615.9 million (USD 6,463.6 million) = USD 946.8 million. The 4.00x level is a reference chosen here, not a target or covenant; nine-month buybacks of USD 916.1 million are of similar size.

6. Excess of buybacks over free cash flow, carried from CP-1: USD 916.1 million less USD 401.5 million = USD 514.6 million. Net debt issuance USD 2,265.0 million less USD 2,041.2 million = USD 223.8 million, as in CP-1.
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Affects | Action |

| Executed indentures, credit agreement and intercreditor terms not supplied (inherited from the source readiness and financial base) | High for legal work, Moderate otherwise | Covenant headroom, restricted payment capacity, guarantor and collateral conclusions | Obtain documents; do not infer legal capacity from the absence of adverse evidence |
| Secured net leverage ratio not reported; credit agreement EBITDA definition unexplained | Moderate | Covenant conclusions | Obtain the compliance certificate |
| Cash interest paid is available only for FY2025 | Low | Cash-basis interest cover | Use company-reported coverage on interest expense, net, labelled as such |
| Ownership table, control rights and any rating or agency view not in the pack | Moderate | Governance and external-view conclusions | State Not supplied; obtain the 2026 Proxy Statement |

| No data after June 30, 2026 other than buybacks to August 5, 2026 and narrowed guidance | Moderate | Currentness of leverage and liquidity at the as-of date | Label all figures as of June 30, 2026 |
| Adjusted EBITDA is management's non-GAAP measure; the credit agreement adjustment of (18.6) is unexplained | Moderate | Leverage level | Show adjusted and unadjusted bases together, as above |

| Status and revision history: the synthesis is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS, inheriting the readiness status of the earlier handoffs; the financial base corrected the earlier wording on the covenant numerator, and the business handoff corrected the integration-cost wording; this synthesis relies on those corrected statements | Informational | CP-5 trace | CP-5 should check that no module repeats the earlier wording |
## Next module

Proceed to CP-5 (evidence trace validation). It should test that each figure here matches the financial base handoff exactly, that each business statement matches its tagged category in the business handoff, and that the covenant and add-back statements carry the corrections noted above. The sensitivity and illustrative figures in the calculations are derived here and should be recomputed from the cited inputs.
